assessments.reasoning: Section 14.3.1.1 states a Syntax Error when the LexicalBinding’s Initializer is absent and IsConstantDeclaration of the containing LexicalDeclaration is true. Section 8.2.3 makes that predicate true for const. The shared syntax production marks Initializer optional to admit let. Static semantics reject the exact missing-initializer const alternative before evaluation. The requirement comes from the early-error rule. The exact production is a plain BindingIdentifier in a const LexicalDeclaration. The grammar for a bare declaration in for-in or for-of uses ForDeclaration and ForBinding instead. Optional shared syntax does not override early errors. The loop’s const binding goes through a different production. The corrigendum replaces the copyright notice and contains no change to §14.3.1.1 or §8.2.3.

challenge.method: Compare the optional grammar marker with the Early Errors rule and IsConstantDeclaration. Trace an apparent counterexample such as for (const item of items) through ForDeclaration/ForBinding. Inspect the publisher’s edition corrigendum.

limitations: A for-in or for-of declaration uses a different grammar production. The claim does not freeze objects assigned to const bindings.
This assertion is about ordinary plain identifier declaration syntax. Destructuring has its own grammar production and for-in/of has distinct declaration productions.
The obligation concerns initialization of the binding, with object mutability outside the asserted rule.
